claims.claim_vi: Source: MVC is the oldest pattern, almost 50 years old; every pattern has a view for displaying content and receiving input; most have a model for business data; controller, presenter and view-model are translators between view and model ('entity' in VIPER); the translators can be complex to write so variants were proposed to make them more maintainable. The question also names MVVM-C but no bullet explains it.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Apple (Cocoa Core Competencies, retired document): MVC assigns objects the roles model, view or controller; a controller is an intermediary between view objects and model objects; user actions in views go through a controller to the model; when a model changes, a controller communicates the new data to the views; model objects should ideally have no explicit connection to the views. The page notes it may not represent current best practice.
claims.section: Model Objects, View Objects, Controller Objects

claims.claim_vi: Microsoft (.NET MAUI MVVM guide): the view knows the view model and the view model knows the model, not the reverse; unit tests for the view model and the model can be written without the view; the view model should define whether a command is available and the view should bind to it instead of enabling or disabling UI elements in code-behind; view models should not reference view types.
claims.section: Model-View-ViewModel; Connecting view models to views
claims.verified_by: File fetched from the main branch on 2026-10-19 and read.

claims.claim_vi: Experiment: the same counter screen (plus, minus, text 'Count: n', minus enabled only when n > 0, n never below 0) written four times. Classes: MVC 3, MVP 3, MVVM 3, VIPER 5; lines 19, 18, 21, 27. What the middle class touches on the view: MVC two fields, MVP and VIPER one method, MVVM nothing. Objects built to test the minus rule: MVC model and controller, MVP model and presenter, MVVM model and view model, VIPER entity, interactor and presenter; all but MVVM need a fake view. Adding a Reset button changes 3 of 3 classes plus the builder in MVC, MVP, MVVM (8, 11, 8 lines added or removed) and 3 of 5 in VIPER (11 lines; the entity is unchanged). Click-to-text time 0.3 to 0.8 microseconds in all four, order changing between runs.
claims.verified_by: Program run by the author on 2026-10-19; counts are deterministic and were identical in three runs.

design_notes_vi: Ba khung: bốn mẫu chia việc ra sao, đếm trên một màn hình viết bốn lần, giới hạn của đồ chơi.
source_deviations: The source is a picture with five short bullets and no examples; the lesson keeps the bullets, adds independent references for MVC and MVVM, and adds a small program written four times.
MVP and VIPER have no independent reference; MVVM-C is named in the source question but not explained, so the lesson does not cover it.
